headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: LightAgent’s MCP/tooling can ingest Dexter outputs, while both agents have broad egress and overlapping write surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent exposes MCP/stdin-stdout and runtime hooks that can observe or replace lifecycle payloads, so it may ingest Dexter-produced content as trusted input. Dexter’s autonomous execution and file scratchpad increase the chance its outputs are reused without provenance. The pairwise bridge is plausible, but direct hijack evidence is absent.
conditions: IF Dexter output is copied into LightAgent prompts, MCP messages, or stdin/stdout without provenance tags, injection becomes reachable.
IF LightAgent runtime hooks are configured to rewrite payloads, attacker-controlled text from Dexter can be promoted to instructions.
mitigations: Add explicit provenance markers to all Dexter outputs before passing them to LightAgent.
Disable any LightAgent hook that rewrites inbound payloads.
Route inter-agent messages through a read-only handoff file.
Manually inspect any Dexter-generated text before LightAgent executes it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter handles financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys; LightAgent touches conversations, memory, traces, tool results, and provenance metadata, and also has broad egress. If Dexter artifacts enter LightAgent’s context or workspace, sensitive data can be exfiltrated to third-party APIs in default workflows. The pairwise leakage path is credible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Dexter scratchpad files or outputs contain financial data and are loaded into LightAgent context, leakage is reachable.
IF LightAgent forwards tool results or memory to external APIs, copied Dexter data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep Dexter scratchpad and LightAgent workspace on separate directories.
Block LightAgent from reading Dexter files except via a sanitized export.
Rotate any API keys that may have been exposed in shared logs.
Disable external API calls for LightAgent during cross-agent handoff.
Review outbound requests for financial-data fields before enabling network egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad network egress, and Dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad while LightAgent can use subprocesses and MCP. That creates overlapping mutable surfaces where concurrent runs can race on shared files or shared APIs. No locking or isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory, file races on scratchpad or artifacts are reachable.
IF both agents mutate the same external API-backed resource without locks, write conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Run only one writer at a time for shared resources.
Disable subprocess spawning in LightAgent for shared-state tasks.
Use per-agent API credentials where possible.
Add a simple lock file around any shared artifact.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent’s tool-calling and workflow-state handling make it likely to act on upstream text, while Dexter is an autonomous research agent that can emit unverified outputs. If LightAgent treats Dexter’s results as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream tool calls or documents. The profiles do not prove blind trust, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF Dexter outputs are fed into LightAgent without a verification step, erroneous facts can propagate.
IF LightAgent uses Dexter-generated text as tool-call arguments, downstream actions can be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between Dexter and LightAgent.
Require LightAgent to cite source URLs before acting on Dexter outputs.
Compare Dexter outputs against a second source before execution.
Restrict LightAgent to read-only actions when consuming Dexter results.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while LightAgent handles conversations, memory, traces, and provenance metadata. If the pair is used on regulated financial records or customer conversations, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the two systems. No compliance controls are documented, so the mismatch risk is real but not proven severe.
conditions: IF regulated financial records are routed through both agents, retention and audit obligations must be aligned.
IF LightAgent stores traces longer than Dexter stores scratchpad data, deletion requests can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Document which data classes each agent may process.
Set matching retention windows for both agents.
Exclude regulated records from cross-agent workflows.
Log deletion/export requests in one shared register.
Review residency and DPA terms before enabling production use.
